title: Storm
summary: OTYKEN combines Indigenous Siberian musical traditions with modern rock and electronic sounds. “Storm” features lyrics reported to be in Khakas, a language spoken in Siberia. Listen for jaw harp, string instruments, drums, and throat singing.

title: Sumer Is Icumen In (Summer Has Arrived)
summary: “Sumer Is Icumen In” is a medieval English round from the 1200s, sung in Middle English. Four voices enter with the same melody at different times, while two lower voices repeat a pattern. The lyrics celebrate summer and the cuckoo’s call.

title: Sztoj pa moru (Што й па мору – Out There on the Sea)
style: Traditional Belarusian folk song / Polyphonic folk singing
summary: Polish group Laboratorium Pieśni performs a traditional Belarusian folk song using polyphony, with several vocal parts sounding together. Layered voices and drums accompany a story about swans, an eagle, and scattered feathers.

title: Ib Ob Peb, Los Seev Cev (One, Two, Three, Let's Dance)
summary: Hmong American singer Douachi Yang performs an upbeat Hmong-language dance song. The title means “One, Two, Three, Let’s Dance!” A steady pop beat accompanies a group line dance. Filmed in Minnesota, the video celebrates Hmong language and community.

title: We're Back (Te Vaka Version)
artist: Olivia Foa‘i, Sulata Foai-Amiatu & Te Vaka
summary: Olivia Foa‘i, Sulata Foai-Amiatu, and Te Vaka perform this song from Moana 2 in Gagana Tokelau. Polynesian rhythms and wooden log drums accompany a celebration of voyaging and Pacific connections. The video was filmed in New Zealand and Hawaiʻi.

title: Arday Baan Ahayoo (I Am a Student)
summary: “Arday Baan Ahayoo” (“I Am a Student”) is a well-known Somali school song dating to the 1960s. Its lyrics encourage learning and describe students as the country’s “flowers” and the morning’s “light.” This 2024 version is by Astaan Ubad.

title: La Batucada Más Grande del Mundo (The World's Largest Batucada)
summary: Colombian group AAINJAA performs batucada, an energetic drumming style rooted in Afro-Brazilian samba. Drums such as the deep surdo, snare-like caixa, and repinique create interlocking rhythms. The performance combines percussion with coordinated movement.

title: Afrika Hey
artist: Ndlovu Youth Choir, Sun-El Musician & Kenza
summary: South Africa’s Ndlovu Youth Choir joins electronic music producers Sun-El Musician and Kenza in “Afrika Hey,” a celebration of Africa and its people. The song blends layered choral harmonies with Afro-house dance beats, and its video features dancing in Johannesburg.

title: Why
style: Indigenous hip-hop / Contemporary Native American fusion
summary: Supaman is an Apsáalooke (Crow) hip-hop musician from Montana. In “Why,” he uses looping to build layers of sound and explores injustice, hope, and change. Acosia Red Elk, from the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation, performs jingle dress dancing, a tradition connected to healing.

title: One Day
summary: In 2018, Koolulam brought about 3,000 people together in Haifa to sing Matisyahu’s “One Day” in Hebrew, Arabic, and English. The three languages help share a message of peace across communities. Sign language interpreter Chen Hayat makes the message more accessible. Listen for layered choral harmonies.

title: Malagueña
style: Cuban classical piano / Spanish-inspired concert music
summary: Cuban composer Ernesto Lecuona wrote “Malagueña” for his Andalucía piano suite, inspired by the music of southern Spain. The title refers to Málaga, a city in Andalusia. In Anat Navarro’s instrumental performance, listen for dramatic changes in tempo, volume, and melody.

title: さくら (Sakura – Cherry Blossoms)
style: Traditional Japanese folk song / Contemporary koto arrangement
summary: “Sakura Sakura” is a well-known Japanese song celebrating cherry blossoms in spring. Originally used to teach koto, it appeared in a music collection in 1888. Kasumi Watanabe performs her own arrangement on a modern 25-string koto, blending a traditional melody with expressive plucked-string sounds.

title: Jalikunda African Drums (Live Performance)
style: Senegalese drumming / West African traditional music
summary: Jalikunda African Drums shares Senegalese drumming and dance traditions. The musicians use drums such as the djembe to create interlocking rhythms—different patterns that fit together. West African jali (griots) help preserve community histories and stories through music.

musicWords.note: Means “song” or “singing,” rather than all kinds of music.

title: Malhari
style: Bollywood film music / Indian celebratory dance
summary: “Malhari” is a victory celebration from the 2015 Bollywood film Bajirao Mastani, set in 18th-century India. Singer Vishal Dadlani provides the voice while actor Ranveer Singh dances on screen. Powerful drum rhythms, energetic singing, and synchronized choreography celebrate the Maratha warriors’ victory.

musicWords.note: Means “music” in both Hindi and Marathi.

title: Aku Mahi (My Work)
summary: “Aku Mahi” is a Māori waiata by Kōhine Pōnika celebrating the performing arts passed down through generations. Its lyrics mention haka, poi, action songs, and traditional weapons. Singing and coordinated movements express pride in Māori culture and the importance of preserving ancestral knowledge.

title: El Derecho de Vivir en Paz (The Right to Live in Peace)
summary: “The Right to Live in Peace” was written by Chilean musician Víctor Jara. Later artists recorded it to call for peace and justice.

title: Warra Boolee
summary: Sona Takele sings in Afaan Oromoo, an Ethiopian language. “Warra Boolee” blends modern pop with Oromo musical influences.

title: Are You Ready
summary: Nive Nielsen is an Inuk singer from Greenland who often plays a small red ukulele. This video was filmed during a very cold winter in Uummannaq.

title: Beautiful Karen (กะเหรี่ยง – Karen People)
artist: Debary feat. Toh Pah Doh, Bee Yang & Sa Kaw
summary: “Beautiful Karen” celebrates Karen communities in Myanmar, Thailand, and beyond. Debary and featured artists combine modern pop with Karen cultural expression.

title: Hakuna Matata (Jambo Bwana – Hello, Sir)
summary: “Jambo Bwana” is a Kenyan welcome song. Listen for Swahili greetings including “jambo” (hello) and “hakuna matata” (no worries).

title: يما ويا يابي (Yamma W Ya Yabi – Oh, My Mother and Father)
summary: Syrian band Takkat performs a modern arrangement of a traditional Arabic song, blending older musical heritage with contemporary sounds.

title: É Proibido Cochilar (Sleeping Is Forbidden)
summary: “É Proibido Cochilar” means “No Sleeping Allowed.” Mari Campolongo performs this lively Brazilian forró song with an asalato, a handheld percussion instrument.

title: Tinikling (Traditional Filipino Bamboo Dance)
summary: Tinikling is a Filipino folk dance in which dancers time their steps between moving bamboo poles. The poles make a rhythm of their own.

title: Hip-Hop Tinikling (Modern Filipino Bamboo Dance)
summary: This performance adds a contemporary hip-hop style to Filipino tinikling. Watch how dancers coordinate with the moving bamboo poles.

title: Lead with Love
summary: Melanie DeMore's “Lead with Love” is about persistence, hope, and supporting one another. Its repeating words invite everyone to sing.

title: ព្រោះតែអូន (Because of You)
summary: Vann Lida performs a cover of a song associated with Cambodian singer Sinn Sisamouth. A cover is a new performance of an existing song.

title: Sail (AWOLNATION Rework)
summary: MEUTE is a German techno marching band. Its brass and percussion instruments recreate sounds often associated with electronic dance music.

title: Carnaval de Mi Tierra (Carnival of My Homeland)
summary: Los Hermanos Lovo play chanchona music from El Salvador. Their song celebrates the carnival of San Miguel, with violins and a large string bass.

title: Playing God
summary: Polyphia is an instrumental rock band known for intricate guitar playing. “Playing God” combines acoustic-style guitar sounds and modern rhythms.

title: Classical Dragon
summary: Tim Henson and Marcin bring together different guitar-playing techniques. Watch how they make both melodies and rhythms with their instruments.

title: Could You Be Loved
summary: Bob Marley & The Wailers combine reggae and disco influences in “Could You Be Loved,” a song about love and being true to yourself.

title: Get Up, Stand Up
summary: Bob Marley's reggae song “Get Up, Stand Up” encourages listeners to speak up for their rights. Listen for the repeated chorus and rhythmic groove.

title: Soul Makossa
summary: Cameroonian musician Manu Dibango made “Soul Makossa” famous. Makossa is dance music from Cameroon; listen for saxophone, funk, and jazz influences.

title: Con Gái Miền Tây (Girl from the Mekong Delta)
summary: Vietnamese singer Lương Khánh Vy performs a song connected with the Mekong Delta, a region known for rivers, canals, and boats.

title: أنا مش فاكر الكوبليه (Ana Msh Faker El Kobleh – I Can't Remember the Verse)
summary: Egyptian musician G.oka performs mahraganat, a high-energy electronic street-music style. The playful title means “I don't remember the verse!”

title: Los que se quedan, los que se van (Those Who Stay, Those Who Leave)
summary: Venezuelan band Desorden Público sings about people who leave their homeland and those who remain. The song expresses sadness and hope for reunion.

title: የኔ አበሻ (Yene Habesha – My Habesha)
summary: Abby Lakew sings in Amharic and celebrates Ethiopian culture. Watch for shoulder movements connected with the Ethiopian dance eskista.

title: Walallay
summary: Afrikaan Ali shares music connected with the Afar people of Ethiopia and nearby countries. Listen for rhythmic clapping and singing.

musicWords.note: Means “song” in Afar, rather than music in general.

title: ወኒ (Weni)
summary: “Weni” is a 2018 Tigrinya-language music video by Ethiopian singer Timnit Welday. Listen for the vocal melody, steady rhythmic accompaniment, and the relationship between the singing and dancing.

title: Vuelvo (I'm Coming Back)
summary: “Vuelvo” means “I return.” Nicaraguan reggae musician Philip Montalbán explores connections to home, family, and Afro-Caribbean culture.

title: Dashain Aayo (Dashain Has Arrived)
artist: Prabin Bajracharya, Praanjal Bajracharya & Ramita Adhikari
summary: “Dashain Aayo” means “Dashain has arrived!” This song celebrates an important festival in Nepal.

title: Larsha Pekhawar (Go to Peshawar)
artist: Ali Zafar feat. Gul Panra & Fortitude Pukhtoon Core
summary: “Larsha Pekhawar” means “Go to Peshawar.” This Pashto-language performance combines singing and rap; listen for the rubab string instrument.

title: Marryuna (Dancing)
summary: Baker Boy is an Aboriginal Australian rapper who performs in Yolŋu Matha and English. “Marryuna” celebrates dance and language.

musicWords.note: Means “song” or “music.” Manikay also refers to traditional Yolŋu songs that share ancestral stories and connections to Country.

title: Bugambilia (Bougainvillea)
summary: Colombian group Nasa Histoires blends pop and jazz. The bougainvillea flower in “Bugambilia” represents hope during difficult feelings.

title: Deora
artist: Pritom Hasan, Fazlu Majhi, Palakar & Ghaashphoring Choir (Coke Studio Bangla)
summary: Bangladeshi musician Pritom Hasan blends modern pop with traditional boat-racing song influences. “Deora” celebrates teamwork and energy.

title: Oye Cómo Va (Listen to How It Goes)
style: Cha-cha-chá, Latin rock, and Latin fusion
summary: “Oye Cómo Va” was written and first recorded in 1962 by Tito Puente, a New York-born musician of Puerto Rican heritage. The song draws on cha-cha-chá, a dance-music style from Cuba. Santana, a U.S. rock band led by Mexican-born guitarist Carlos Santana, made it famous with a Latin rock version in 1970. In this Playing for Change performance, musicians from around the world come together to play the song, combining Latin rhythms, percussion, electric guitar, and other musical influences.

title: Koi Ladki Hai (There Is a Girl)
artist: Lata Mangeshkar & Udit Narayan (from Dil To Pagal Hai)
facts: From the 1997 film Dil To Pagal Hai
The title means ‘There Is a Girl.’
The song playfully connects laughter and singing with monsoon rain.
Playback singers record the vocals heard while actors perform onscreen.
summary: “Koi Ladki Hai” is a Hindi film song from Dil To Pagal Hai. Lata Mangeshkar and Udit Narayan sing while actors perform on screen.

title: Montuno
facts: From the 1993 album Mi Tierra (‘My Homeland’).
Written by Cuban musician Juanito Márquez.
Son montuno uses repeating musical patterns, percussion, and call and response.
The lyrics celebrate music, dancing, and community.
summary: Gloria Estefan's “Montuno” celebrates Cuban son montuno, with repeating instrumental patterns, percussion, and call and response.

title: Dúlaman (Seaweed)
summary: “Dúlaman” is a traditional Irish-language song about seaweed. Celtic Woman's arrangement features singer Lisa Lambe.

title: Maskara (مسكرة)
summary: Saint Levant and Mohammed Assaf perform Palestinian Arabic pop. The video features dabkeh, a group dance with synchronized steps and stomps.

title: S.O.S.
summary: French singer Indila's “S.O.S.” is about feeling lost and calling out for help. Listen for the emotion in her voice.

title: Taiko Drumming Performance (The Late Show with Stephen Colbert)
facts: DRUM TAO is a taiko drumming group from Japan.
Wadaiko are Japanese drums of different shapes and sizes.
The group combines drumming, coordinated movement, and dance.
Drums have been used in Japan for centuries at festivals and performances.
summary: DRUM TAO is a Japanese taiko ensemble. Its performers combine powerful wadaiko drums, coordinated rhythms, and movement.

title: Finess
facts: Video link needs correction: spreadsheet currently points to DRUM TAO.
summary: Michael Prince's contemporary performance invites you to notice the connections among rhythm, singing, and movement.

title: Liquindi (Baka Water Drumming)
facts: Women and girls make rhythms by striking the water surface.
Ostinato means a repeating musical pattern.
Polyphony means multiple different musical lines sounding together.
summary: Liquindi is a Baka water-drumming tradition from Central Africa. Women and girls strike the water to make interlocking rhythms.

musicWords.note: Means “song” or “to sing” in documented Baka usage; Baka water drumming is instrumental.

title: Desafinado (Out of Tune)
summary: “Desafinado” means “out of tune.” This bossa nova song playfully answers critics; listen for gentle guitar rhythms and jazz-influenced melody.

title: Love Song (Inuit Throat Singing)
summary: Inuit throat singing often involves two performers exchanging short rhythmic sounds. Listen for breath, repetition, and playful interaction.

title: Dirree (Dire Dawa)
summary: Kemer Yousuf performs in Afaan Oromoo, a language spoken in Ethiopia. Listen for Oromo-language singing and contemporary sounds.

title: Tjovane (The Thieves)
summary: Spokanki performs “Tjovane,” a Norwegian story song about thieves, with layered voices, frame drums, and tambourine.

title: Nour El Ain (نور العين – Light of My Eyes)
summary: Egyptian singer Amr Diab's “Nour El Ain” means “light of my eyes.” The Arabic pop song blends guitar and dance rhythms.
